claims.text: Greg Short asserts that consistent sleep timing — going to bed and waking at the same time every day, allowing at most one hour of deviation — is the foundational physical and mental health behavior for entrepreneurs. Having personally experimented with a wide range of health protocols, he identifies sleep schedule regularity as the single most important lever, on top of which diet and exercise produce meaningful effects.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Entrepreneurs managing high cognitive and emotional load
Applies as a baseline anchor before layering diet or exercise optimizations
claims.mechanism: Regularity of the sleep-wake cycle stabilizes downstream biological and cognitive function; without this anchor, diet and exercise interventions produce inconsistent results.
bounded_by: Up to one hour of deviance is tolerated without disrupting the benefit
Does not specify minimum sleep duration — only timing consistency

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that the specific type of physical activity is irrelevant to the health benefit for entrepreneurs; any consistent movement — whether 15,000 daily steps, heavy weightlifting, running, or rowing — delivers comparable benefit. The critical variable is choosing a form of movement and sustaining it, not optimizing the modality.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Entrepreneurs seeking physical and mental health maintenance
Applies when the goal is baseline wellbeing rather than athletic performance

numbers.axis: Daily step count as one valid movement proxy

anchors.value: heavy weightlifting, no rep minimum stated

bounded_by: Speaker does not claim equivalence for athletic performance outcomes, only general health maintenance

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that maintaining combined lifestyle habits — consistent sleep timing, quality diet, and daily physical activity — for approximately two months produces a physical and mental transformation dramatic enough that the person will not recognize themselves. The implication is that single-day or short-duration compliance is insufficient; the compounding effect requires sustained multi-month commitment.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: All three habits (sleep consistency, diet quality, daily movement) maintained simultaneously
Duration of at least approximately two months required for the transformation threshold
claims.mechanism: Compounding biological adaptations across sleep, nutrition, and movement require weeks of consistent inputs before they produce observable external changes.

numbers.axis: Duration of habit consistency required for noticeable transformation

bounded_by: Based on Greg Short's personal self-report; no cohort comparison or baseline measurement cited
Specific transformation magnitude is unquantified beyond the colloquial 'won't recognize yourself'

examples.text: Greg Short describes arriving at his current health protocol only after experimenting with a wide range of interventions. After trying many approaches, he settled on three pillars — same-time sleep and wake every day with up to one hour of flexibility, high-protein diet with quality fats and carbs from fruits and meat (with personal preference away from vegetables), and any consistent physical movement. His conclusion is that sustaining this combined protocol for a couple of months produced a dramatic enough physical and mental change that he uses the phrase 'won't even recognize yourself in the mirror' to capture the magnitude.

practices.text: Eat high-protein with quality fats and quality carbohydrates sourced from fruits and meat. Greg Short personally avoids large quantities of vegetables and finds this dietary pattern keeps him sharp, though he frames this as personal preference rather than a universal prescription.

Spend meaningful time outdoors under natural sunlight each day. Greg Short reports that natural vitamin D exposure makes him feel significantly better and tries to arrange a portion of his day outside.
